quick_skim.title: Small sums of roots of unity: polylogarithmic exceptional sets and conditional separation
quick_skim.abstract: We prove a polylogarithmic exceptional-set estimate for symmetric five-term sums of roots of unity of arbitrary order. More precisely, at most $O((\log(2N))^{11})$ points of the $N$-grid satisfy $|1+2\cos(2πx)+2\cos(2πy)|<\exp(-C(\log(2N))^{13})$. This implies the corresponding bound for small conjugates at the reduced conductor: outside polylogarithmically many real embeddings, every such sum is at least quasipolynomially large. The proof is unconditional and combines a polynomial-vector-field multiplicity estimate, arithmetic jet determinants, analytic propagation, and interpolation determinants for nearby grid points. As a companion result, assuming a uniform number-field $abc$ conjecture, we prove that every sum of a fixed number of distinct prime-order roots of unity has modulus at least $\exp(-\varepsilon p)$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large primes $p$, uniformly in the exponents. That proof uses simultaneous compression of the exponents, discriminant estimates, and cyclic resultants.

quick_skim.title: The $A_3$ Narain family over $\mathbb{Z}_4$
quick_skim.abstract: The code $\{000,220,202,022\}\subset\mathbb{Z}_4^3$ realizes the split $A_3$ root-weight gluing construction as ordinary Construction A, preserving the Lorentzian pairing and the positive energy form. For two hyperbolic pairs of $A_3$ blocks, the twenty-two even self-dual gluing codes form seven block-monomial classes. Explicit metric and $B$-field representatives and theta series distinguish exactly seven T-duality classes in this family at central charge six; the one-pair family has two classes at central charge three. For arbitrary $d$, the chiral root system on either side is $A_1^{3m}$, where $m$ counts the words $(2e_i,2e_i)$ in the gluing code. Exactly one two-pair class has no zero-$B$ T-duality frame. Intersections of gluing codes determine finite shift orbifolds between the backgrounds, with the target code specifying the twisted-sector projections.

quick_skim.title: Lattice Moduli and Residual Atoms
quick_skim.abstract: We study prescribed holomorphic lattices for regular-singular connections and residual factors of quantum $F$-bundles. For an arbitrary ordered monodromy spectrum, we classify the fully framed local groupoid: each residue fibre is a discrete affine space of dimension $r(r-1)$, with a unique normal form and trivial stabilisers. We then analyse elementary changes of lattice. A strictly positive integral residue difference obstructs the oriented wall; otherwise, in arbitrary rank, the extending normal-form arcs form an affine torsor of relative dimension $r(r-1)$, and specialisation to the shifted residue slice is polynomial and triangular by root height. Adjacent walls exhibit the composite-root correction dictated by the type-$A$ root-subgroup relations, while an example over the dual numbers detects a nilpotent saturation defect. For one-branch $F$-bundles, the scalar branch is recovered from the residual trace, and scalar residualisation yields a symmetric monoidal equivalence with zero-branch $F$-bundles. This construction yields residual atoms, functorial Jordan strata, and a residual chemical formula compatible with blow-ups and projective bundles. In the $A$-model, residualisation removes the unit direction; the rationally marked large-radius residual germ recovers the divisor cubic and distinguishes the marked residual germs of the Pfaffian and Grassmannian Calabi--Yau threefolds.

quick_skim.title: Elementary-Symmetric Ricci Gravity: Metric Formulation
quick_skim.abstract: We investigate a four-dimensional metric theory of gravity whose Lagrangian is a linear combination of the elementary symmetric polynomials of the Ricci tensor. We derive the field equations and characterize Einstein vacua and a real, diagonalizable class of parallel-Ricci vacua. The latter includes direct products of two constant-curvature surfaces and can exhibit a hierarchy of curvature radii. The Einstein vacua possess multiple branches associated with the distinct roots of a polynomial, whose multiple roots define boundaries in parameter space. We derive the linearized equations on maximally symmetric backgrounds, distinguish the scalar and spin-2 degrees of freedom, and then analyze their classical linear stability. We also obtain the generalized Friedmann constraint and the associated homogeneous evolution equations. An illustrative spatially flat solution evolves from the neighborhood of an unstable de Sitter solution toward a stable de Sitter solution. This behavior may motivate further investigation into early- and late-time accelerated expansion and provide a gravity-driven mechanism for automatic end of inflation.

quick_skim.title: Beta-expansions induced by general Parry polynomials and sharp iteration asymptotics of their transfer operators
quick_skim.abstract: This paper generalizes previous results to any Parry polynomials $p_n(z)$ \cite{Pa} of finite degree $n\geq 2$. Let $β>1$ be the unique positive root of $p_n$ and consider the transfer operator $\mathscr{P}$ induced by the map $[0,1]\ni x\mapsto βx-\lfloor βx\rfloor \in [0,1)$. Suppose all other roots of $p_n$ have magnitude less than one. Then for any smooth function $F$ on $[0,1]$ we prove two term asymptotics in $L^\infty$ of the form \begin{equation*}   \big(\mathscr{P}^r(F)\big)(\cdot)= u(\cdot) \int_0^1 F(x)\: \mathrm{d} x +β^{-r}v(\cdot) \big (F(1)-F(0)\big )+o(β^{-r}),\quad r\geq 1, \end{equation*} where $u$ is piecewise constant and $\mathscr{P}u=u$, while $v$ is piecewise equal to a polynomial of degree one and $\mathscr{P}v= β^{-1}v$.   When $\mathscr{P}$ is restricted to functions of bounded variation $BV([0,1])$, it is known that $\vert z \vert\leq β^{-1}$ contains its essential spectrum. Thus the contribution coming from $v$ in the above estimate is not guaranteed if $F$ is not smooth enough.   Furthermore, we show that when $\mathscr{P}$ is restricted to $BV([0,1])$ then any $\vert z \vert<β^{-1}$ is an eigenvalue with infinite multiplicity. Moreover, we construct a meromorphic extension of $(\mathscr{P}-z)^{-1}$ to the domain $\vert z \vert>β^{-1}$, where the finite rank poles are numbers $ζ$ with $β^{-1}<\vert ζ\vert\leq 1$ such that $βζ$ is a root of $p_n(z)$. If such poles $ζ$ other than $1$ exist, then we construct eigenvectors of $\mathscr{P}^*$ in $BV^*$ obeying $\mathscr{P}^*\hat{U}=ζ\hat{U}$, where $\hat{U}(F)$ is given by series involving the values of $F$ taken in some specially chosen, finer and finer partitions of $[0,1]$. When $F$ is either a polynomial or a characteristic function like $χ_{[0,x]}$, then $\hat{U}(F)$ can be explicitly computed.

quick_skim.title: Hodge Theory of Novikov Type Landau--Ginzburg Models
quick_skim.abstract: We establish a strong Hodge decomposition theorem for Novikov type Landau--Ginzburg models, that is, triples $(M,g,θ)$ consisting of a non-compact complete Kähler manifold $(M,g)$ and a non-trivial closed holomorphic one-form $θ$ on $M$.Under the well-tameness condition and under the assumption that $M$ is Stein, we prove that the space of $L^{2}$-forms on $M$ admits an orthogonal decomposition into the space of harmonic forms of the twisted Laplacian $Δ_θ$ and the images of the twisted Dolbeault operators $\bar\partial+θ\wedge$ and $\bar\partial^{\dagger}+ι_{\barθ^{\sharp}}$; moreover, the harmonic space is concentrated in degree $n=\dim_{\C}M$ and is isomorphic to the Milnor rings of $θ$.   As applications, we endow the complement of a hyperplane arrangement with a complete cylindrical Kähler metric, and we show that the differential of a master function with nonresonant weights is well-tamed with respect to this metric. After passing to a log resolution in the non-normal-crossing case; we then apply the results to the Yang--Yang functional of the Gaudin model, whose critical points are the Bethe roots: the top-degree harmonic space is described by the corresponding Milnor rings, and the number of Bethe roots is given by the Varchenko--Orlik--Terao lattice formula.

quick_skim.title: Semantic Observability for Autonomous Systems Diagnostics
quick_skim.abstract: Modern distributed microservice deployments generate massive volumes of heterogeneous, multi-format observability logs across physically and logically partitioned infrastructure. Isolating root causes during cascading failures remains an arduous task for Site Reliability Engineers (SREs), bottlenecked by manual keyword filtering and disjointed temporal correlation across monitoring dashboards. We introduce Semantic Observability, an autonomous multi-agent framework that unifies disparate log streams into a dynamic, queryable Property Graph Database. By modeling physical infrastructure topologies, logical software dependencies, and chronological event sequences as attributed nodes and directed relations, it bridges the semantic gap inherent in flat, unstructured log repositories. Building on this unified substrate, we deploy a stateful multi-agent system orchestrated through Directed Cyclic Graphs (DCGs). The system autonomously navigates the topology, applying causal graph algorithms and temporal back-traversal to isolate the precise blast radius of anomalies. The pruned subgraph is then interpreted by a Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning engine to generate contextualized, code-level Root Cause Analyses (RCA) and actionable remediations. This paper establishes the foundational system architecture, formal relational ontology, and multi-agent control loops of Semantic Observability. We show conceptually how the framework eliminates ambient telemetry noise, reduces Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR), compresses LLM token consumption, and prevents structural hallucinations. We also specify an open-source validation framework on standard benchmarks (LogHub and Train-Ticket), laying the groundwork for a forthcoming companion paper on exhaustive quantitative evaluation and production benchmarking.

quick_skim.title: Rethinking World Models for Biosignals
quick_skim.abstract: World models promise to learn how systems evolve and respond to actions, enabling simulation, planning and decision-making. Bringing this promise to biosignals requires more than accurate prediction of physiological recordings. We examine existing biosignal world models through two requirements for intervention use: a genuine action and evidence of its causal effect. We identify three fundamental bottlenecks rooted in physiology: Temporal Latency, the variable delay between an action and its observable effect; System Openness, the influence of drivers beyond the modelled intervention; and Endogenous Dynamics, the system's ongoing evolution without that intervention. Drawing on published evidence, we outline corresponding research directions and propose an Intervention-Effect Validation Checklist to guide evaluation. The aim is to help the biosignal community realise the core promise of world models by learning the latent mechanisms that govern physiological evolution and responses to interventions.

quick_skim.title: Extending Layered Attestation into ARM Application Run-Times
quick_skim.abstract: Modern mobile and edge platforms provide hardware-backed attestation of application and platform integrity at load-time. However, they offer little support once application execution begins. We present ARA, an Application-Runtime Anchor for ARM that extends this load-time chain of trust into execution. ARA bootstraps from the underlying ARM platform Root of Trust (RoT) through a measured loading chain and establishes an attested protected run-time within the application address space using recently introduced ARM Permission Overlay Extensions (POE). The resulting run-time domain can host programmable RoTs for Measurement and Storage (RTM/RTS), enabling application run-time integrity verification, attestation evidence generation, and protected use of secrets while retaining efficient access to application run-time state. As exemplary uses, we instantiate ARA for protected media decryption and application control flow measurement. Our prototype and evaluation show that ARA supports frequent run-time RoT-backed operations at near in-process cost, with roughly 10x and 50x lower overhead than out-of-process equivalents. This offers a practical bridge from layered attestation to application run-time trusted computing on ARM.

quick_skim.title: Least-Squares Finite Element Methods with Weakly Imposed Boundary Conditions: Norm and Error Equivalences, Over-Penalization, and Fully Discontinuous Discretizations
quick_skim.abstract: Weakly imposed boundary conditions in first-order system least-squares methods go back to Jespersen (1977), but two questions have remained open for decades: the right weights, especially for the Neumann residual, whose natural norm $H^{-1/2}$ suggests $h_F$, and norm and error equivalences, especially for indefinite equations. We answer both for general, possibly indefinite, second-order elliptic equations with non-homogeneous mixed boundary conditions. First, for the weights $h_F^{-1}$ on the Dirichlet and $1$ on the Neumann residual, we prove norm and error equivalences with mesh-independent constants for every discrete pair: the error in a mesh-dependent norm is equivalent to the square root of the functional plus a Dirichlet data term. The least-squares solution converges optimally in $H(\mathrm{div};Ω)\times H^{1}(Ω)$, and the functional is a reliable and efficient error estimator, with a recovered flux also for approximations from other methods, even ones violating the boundary conditions. The key idea is to apply the stability of the boundary value problem to pairs that are discrete only in their Dirichlet traces, whose $H^{1/2}$ norm an inverse inequality bounds by the weighted penalty. Second, these weights are the right ones: weaker powers, including $h_F$ on the Neumann boundary, destroy the norm equivalence, and stronger weights are admissible, since the penalty multiplies zero at a comparison function meeting the projected data. Third, for the fully discontinuous counterpart, a pure penalty method with both jumps weighted by $h_F^{-1}$, the error equivalence holds for every discrete pair, also for exact fluxes with normal traces not square integrable on interior faces.
